explanation: Generated an eta-configuration EXCLURAD input for W=1.7 GeV, Q2=1.0 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0, phi*=90 deg, with vcut set to -0.1 as requested. Kinematics are physically valid (well above the eta threshold W~1.486 GeV). Warning: the input.dat/examples documentation states that a negative vcut 'sets a cut on v directly rather than v^2', but this is not actually implemented in eta/exclurad.F. In subroutine bornkin (exclurad.F:237-254), the cut is only applied when cutv > 1e-12; any value <= 0, including -0.1, is silently treated identically to vcut=0 (no inelasticity cut at all, vmax left at its full kinematic maximum). This same logic exists unchanged in the pion (upstream) exclurad.F, so it is a longstanding gap in the original 2002 code rather than an eta-fork-specific bug. The run will execute without error and produce valid output, but it will NOT apply any cut on v -- it will be numerically equivalent to vcut=0. If a genuine inelasticity cut is desired, use a small positive vcut (e.g. the CLAS12 default 0.166 GeV^2) instead.
